summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (Jan 2.10/2543)

data.turoyo: <...> An naʕime, d kətne yanoqe, faliti m qəm ṣadrayye w kəzzən bayn dam maye...
data.translation: <...> The children who were suckling infants slipped from in front of their breasts and go among the water...

rationale: First I Part act.; the complete supplied sentence gives the plural referent and breast context. Its source ellipsis is retained. The form may function as an age-class noun rather than assert an action in progress. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; the sense is based on the Turoyo.

data.translation: "Was hast du angefangen? sprich!" "Da war ein Kalb angebunden, die Kuh kam gerade von der Weide, da habe ich es zu seiner Mutter gelassen, und es hat an ihr gesaugt."

data.translation: Die Frauen haben die Gewohnheit, so mit den Händen ihre Brüste zu pressen. Sie sprach: Bruder! Mine Brust hat sich mit Milch gefüllt! - Nun ja, es ist ja ihr Sohn! Der Junge trank.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC NE ezo koviye/13)

data.turoyo: Omar, ‘Rabbane, i+ʕezo+koviye mamṣówayle, hawi rabī́ṭ, maqbele, i+ʕezo+koviye maməṣla, maynaqla, ŭ hawi barmə́lk̇’.
data.translation: He says, ‘Poor thing, the wild nanny goat would suckle him, he became a toddler, he has flourished,  the wild nanny goat suckled him, she nursed him from her teat, and he became an infant’.

rationale: Thin III Preterit cell; full context for maynaqla rather than another isolated form.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (105/120)

data.turoyo: Komər qayimo haṯi w azzala li emo, məllala: “Ya abri, i ḥurmayḏux, d kətyo bu ḥalano, d kətyo bi daraǧaṯi, u ḥalwayḏi howe ḥaram aʕlux w al lalyawoṯe d konən, d qayimono, d monaqlilux w d mḥaramli i šanṯo dal lalyawoṯe aʕlux w d adyawma d tawrat lu xabrayḏi, ḥalwayḏi w taʕbayḏi howe ḥaram aʕlux, howe avzalelkat bi lašayḏux, d l oṯat adyawma, d maḥwat ruḥux li ḥurmaṯi w balki d xəlṣo mi ʕaḏabaṯi.”
data.translation: Die Mutter ging und sprach zu ihm: Mein Sohn, deine Frau, die in diesem Zustand, dem Tode nahe ist. Meine Milch soll für dich verboten, unrein sein, und die Winternächte, in denen ich aufgestanden bin und dich gestillt, wo ich den Nächtlichen Schlaf um deinetwillen von meinem Auge verbannt habe, wenn du jetzt mein Wort mißachtest, so soll meine Milch und all die Mühe, die ich um dich gehabt habe, dir ungesegnet sein, und Eiterheulen sollen an deinem leih aufbrechen, wenn du nicht zu dieser Frau kommst und dich ihr zeigst, damit sie vielleicht aus dieser Qual erlöst wird. -

rationale: Thin III Preterit cell; first-person agent plus second-person patient in monaqlilux.

data.turoyo: W l aloho hawxa ḥzele bu ray w hawi ḥalwo b ṣadrona di ḥurma d Usuf Paša. Komər monaqla u zʕurawo w u zʕurawo hawi rabo.
data.translation: Nach Gottes Ratschluss entstand Milch in den Brüsten der Frau von Jusuf Pascha. Sie säugte den kleinen, und er wurde groß.

summary: All 25 occurrences checked. Stem I takes the suckling creature as agent. The l-marked calf in the existing inəqle i tərto l-u=arwono is the agent, not recipient: the cow is the feeding source/object. Infectum subjects are zero-marked; the source may be m-marked (JTM 1.1/81; PrS 86/22).

PrS 53/33 inəqole appears to encode a feminine source/object before the agent suffix. 96/46 repeats the l-marked boy agent with no overt feeding source. This supplies more secure argument evidence than inferring roles from the translation.

Stem III denotes nursing/suckling another creature. Human and animal caregivers, and children, dogs and kittens as patients, stay within the existing sense. In 59/86 the subject of the desired nursing is the ewes, not the couple who released the lambs.
Printed maynaqla, mənqola, monaqlilux, monaqla and monaqqe are retained as variants of the supplied III paradigm. No new stem is inferred from contraction or apparent nql.

Several PrS passages repeat existing quotations with legacy references: the dog (PrS 28/9), nurse (PrS 43/17), Imperativ (PrS 44/28), calf (PrS 53/26,29). No duplicate passage was added or unverified citation conversion performed.

90/153 is explicitly partial-alignment material: the German adds a maternal untouchability comparison not expressed in the Turoyo. No translation from that row is quoted; milk-kinship interpretation remains a question.
Plural yanoqe in d kətne yanoqe qualifies an naʕime; m qəm ṣadrayye provides the feeding context. It supports the form under I.1 but does not by itself establish a separate lexical infant sense.

Part act. is the glossary box used for this attested shape. Its predicative, potentially nominal use does not show that an instance of sucking was in progress. No patient, feeding source argument of ynq or Detransitive is overt in the relative clause; the breast phrase belongs to faliti.
Confirm -o- in inəqole (PrS 53/33) as feminine source/object before the l-series agent.
Confirm segmentation of monaqqe (85/18), especially q+n assimilation versus another contraction; preserve the transmitted form.
Check maynaqla (MAC NE ezo koviye/13) against mawn-/mon-/mən- variants without silently harmonizing vowels.
Does 90/153 describe literal/ritual milk sucking or conventional milk-kinship language? Resolve its translation alignment before admitting an example.
Reconcile the legacy prs page/line-like references with current PrS text/verse identifiers before changing citations.
Jan 2.10/2543: is yanoqe understood here as a productive Part act. of ynq or as the conventional noun for unweaned infants? Preserve the attested form and I.1 link pending confirmation.
Adults as suckers and milk kinship can extend participants while retaining literal sucking. The partial-alignment 90/153 row is not quoted or promoted into a new ritual sense.
